title: automate-transit-gateway-attachments-and-delegated-private-dns-scope
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Customers deploying Redwood Private across multiple AWS accounts often need Transit Gateway (TGW) attachments for cross-account control plane connectivity and a way to scope private DNS resolution to the control plane without exposing zones broadly. This PR automates TGW attachment creation and tidy delegation of a control-plane-scoped Private Hosted Zone via Route 53 Resolver inbound/outbound endpoints. It also tightens the security group model for control-plane endpoints to default-deny and only allow explicit CIDR/account attachments. Changes summary: 1) New Terraform module modules/networking/tgw/ that encapsulates TGW creation, cross-account attachment role document, and a lifecycle mode that supports create-only (for air-gapped upgrades) or reconcile. 2) Installer top-level deployment wiring to optionally enable tgw_attachments with a mapping of account IDs and attachmentopts. 3) Route53 automation: modules/dns/delegation.tf creates a control-plane PHZ with conditional delegation records, plus resolver rules and endpoint resources that are tied to the TGW attachment's route propagation. 4) Security: modules/sg/controlplane_sg.tf converts existing broad endpoint SGs into a least-privilege set with explicit ingress lists generated from the attachment map, and adds automated rotation hooks for SG references used by the control plane. 5) Helm chart values: values-private.yaml adds feature flags to toggle tgw and resolver automation per-environment. 6) Migration helper script scripts/terraform/migrate-tgw-attachments.sh to import existing TGW attachments and reconcile state with minimal downtime. Testing and validation: Unit-tested the TF modules with local terratest mocks, end-to-end validation in a staging account that simulates cross-account attach (recorded runbook attached). CI: plan/apply guard rails included; CI runs terraform fmt, validate and a mocked plan diff; end-to-end apply validated against a dedicated staging sandbox. Rollout plan: feature is behind the installer flag "enable_cross_account_tgw" and disabled by default; staged rollout recommended for customers with cross-account networking requisites. Rollback: the modules include an explicit variable to turn the lifecycle into "delete_on_disable" false by default; to rollback, flip the flag and run the provided migrate-tgw-attachments.sh to detach with tracked state. Security notes: cross-account IAM role created by the module is narrowly scoped to AttachVpc and RejectTransitGatewayVpcAttachment resources and requires an explicit acceptance token from the owner account. Related work: builds on ENG-988 and the private deployment DNS hardening initiative.
commits: 3 commits: (a) add tgw module and basic wiring, (b) add resolver/delegation module and SG hardening, (c) add migration script and update helm values, plus small followup fix to IAM trust policy after review.

release_notes: Feature: Optional automation to create cross-account Transit Gateway attachments and scoped control-plane private DNS delegation. Notes: Disabled by default, requires cross-account IAM cooperation and network routing review before enabling.
